key_insight: RAD-2 combines diffusion-based trajectory generators with a discriminator-trained reinforcement signal to stabilize stochastic planners and provide corrective feedback in closed-loop driving, yielding more reliable multimodal planning.
problem_solved: Diffusion planners model complex multimodal futures but are unstable and lack negative corrective feedback when trained only by imitation learning, leading to brittle closed-loop behavior in high-level autonomous driving.
method: Use a generator (diffusion-based trajectory sampler) to produce multimodal candidate plans.
Train a discriminator/critic that judges closed-loop rollouts and supplies corrective signals or rewards, enabling reinforcement-style fine-tuning of the generator.
Jointly scale this generator–discriminator loop with closed-loop simulation data to reduce stochastic instabilities and improve robustness.
impact: Provides a practical way for AI/ML practitioners to make generative planners robust in closed-loop control, improving safety and reliability of motion planning for autonomous systems without abandoning expressive multimodal models.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram showing Generator (diffusion) → Candidate trajectories → Environment rollouts → Discriminator → Feedback to Generator

paper_title: RAD-2: Scaling Reinforcement Learning in a Generator-Discriminator Framework
paper_authors: Hao Gao, Shaoyu Chen, Yifan Zhu, Yuehao Song, Wenyu Liu
